topic: Cartagena/SPEC regasification capacity build-up (400 vs 450 baseline; 475 and 533 milestones)
wiki_text: Reported capacity figures for the SPEC (Sociedad Portuaria El Cayao) FSRU terminal at Cartagena differ on the BASELINE and on how the expansion increments are apportioned, though all sources agree on the interim and final targets. Promigas and Vopak took FID in November 2025 to lift regasification capacity by 33% to up to 533 MMscfd; LNG Prime (2025-11-11) describes this as rising 'from a current limit of 400 MMscfd' to 533 MMscfd. The terminal operator's own sources instead state a 450 MMcf/d baseline: the Calamarí (SPEC LNG) facilities page lists '450 MPCD' (millones de pies cúbicos por día) as current capacity, and Valora Analitik (2025-09-04) reported that 'desde el pasado 1 de septiembre la infraestructura pasó de 450 a 475 millones de pies cúbicos por día' — i.e., a first-phase increment of +25 MMcf/d to 475 MMcf/d, effective 1 September 2025. A second phase of +58 MMcf/d (to 533 MMcf/d) is targeted for around August 2027. Reconciling the two framings: (A) 400 + 75 + 58 = 533 (used in GEM's unit build-up and by LNG Prime); (B) 450 + 25 + 58 = 533 (used by SPEC/Calamarí and Valora Analitik). Both reach the same 475 and 533 milestones; the discrepancy is whether the original nameplate is treated as 400 or 450 MMcf/d. The FSRU is the 170,000 m³ Höegh Grace (Höegh Evi/LNG), chartered by SPEC; the charter was extended to at least 2031.
